title: Haj arrangements with Saudi Arabia: quota, queue and health rules for senior pilgrims
asked: Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked how Singapore builds on its working relationship with Saudi authorities on Haj arrangements, covering quota allocation, queue arrangements and health requirements for senior pilgrims.
answered_by: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
response: Singapore has a quota of 900 Haj places and has asked Saudi Arabia for more, most recently in November 2025. MUIS runs the quota through the MyHajSG portal queue on a first-come, first-served basis, with priority for pilgrims aged 70 and above. From 2026, Saudi Arabia will require a valid medical health certificate, and MUIS and the Ministry of Health have worked with local healthcare providers to help pilgrims meet this.

key_points.quote: Saudi Arabia sets the Haj quota for various countries based on a standardised formula, that is 0.1% of each country's Muslim population.
